items.title: Meta’s Generative Ads Model (GEM): Scaling the Central Model and Compute Engine for Frontier Ads AI
items.abstract: Last year, we introduced GEM , the industry’s largest recommendation system (RecSys) foundation model. GEM established Meta’s first LLM-inspired paradigm for ads recommendation, driving major performance gains. Building on this foundation, our next goal is to further scale both compute and intelligence transfer with next-generation hardware, and expand this capability across Meta’s entire ads ecosystem. This spans dozens of surfaces and objectives, delivering seamless full-funnel optimization across awareness, consideration, and conversions. The 2026 generation of GEM shifts from isolated per-domain optimizations — such as Facebook, Instagram, Reels — to a single central foundation model. It learns from data and signals across all of Meta’s ads platforms, bends the scaling curve at LLM-scale computation, and delivers strong advertiser outcomes through post-training techniques that provide a larger latency budget without requiring real-time evaluation of all ad candidates — all on a substantially more efficient training stack. The result is simultaneous ad performance gains across every surface and funnel stage, and deeper understanding that better matches ads to what people are looking for. GEM has delivered 18.9% conversion improvement and 12% ad click-through rate (CTR) improvement across Meta’s ad surfaces and objectives, and additionally contributed 5.8%, 4.1%, and 1.6% conversion uplift on Facebook, Instagram, and off-site conversion for targeted users over the past year. These gains span both upper-funnel surfaces and deep-funnel optimization goals, driving stronger returns for advertisers. GEM advances the frontier of recommender systems in the following four areas: 1. Bending the Scaling Curve, Enabling 2.5x Model Complexity Challenge: Empirical scaling laws demonstrate that model performance predictably improves with compute, parameter, and data size using transformer model architecture. However, recommender system models do not exhibit similar scaling properties with transformer due to massive heterogeneous features and shifting distributions. Solution: We built an LLM-style architecture — Kunlun , co-designed with the latest GPU hardware, to make larger, deeper models substantially more cost-efficient and to enable long-context learning over user engagement history. We observed an LLM-like scaling law at our largest pre-training scale with 2.5x model complexity growth from earlier versions of GEM. The pattern mirrors frontier LLMs: more capacity and longer context produce emergent gains in ranking quality that translate directly into business results. 2. Efficient Intelligence Transfer From GEM to User-Facing Models Challenge: Serving a model at this scale in real time is prohibitively expensive and drives up latency, compromising both user experience and advertiser ROI. Solution: The structured representation, LoopFM , a state-of-the-art post-training technique, transfers GEM’s internal representations and sequential historical memory to downstream models. Through computation sharing, it doubles the intelligence transfer together with the knowledge distillation deployed in the previous version, at no additional compute cost or latency. We also introduced elastic pre-computation ( Solaris ) to harvest the gains from the upstream model. 3. Accelerating the Central Compute Engine With Large-Scale Cross-Surface, Cross-Domain Learning at Meta Ads Scale Challenge: Meta’s apps span dozens of surfaces — Facebook, Instagram, Reels, Stories, and more — with 3.6 billion people using at least one of our apps each day. Each surface and optimization objective previously had its own independent prediction system. As the platform grows in surfaces and objectives, so does the challenge of improving ad performance simultaneously. Solution: GEM accelerates one single, unified compute engine through the central foundation model that jointly predicts clicks and conversions across all surfaces, including Facebook and Instagram, and acro
items.title_ko: Meta GEM 2026, 광고 추천을 단일 중앙 모델로 통합 — 전환율 18.9%·CTR 12% 개선
items.summary: Meta가 자사 광고 추천시스템 파운데이션 모델 GEM의 2026년 버전을 공개했다. 기존에 Facebook, Instagram, Reels 등 각 서비스별로 분리돼 있던 최적화를 하나의 중앙 파운데이션 모델로 통합해 전체 깔때기(인지·고려·전환) 단계를 동시에 최적화한다. 핵심 아키텍처 Kunlun은 GPU 하드웨어와 공동 설계된 LLM 스타일 구조로, **2.5배 모델 복잡도 증가**에서도 LLM과 유사한 스케일링 법칙을 확인했다. 또한 LoopFM이라는 사후학습 기법으로 GEM의 내부 표현과 사용자 이력 정보를 실시간 서빙 모델에 추가 연산·지연 없이 전달한다. 그 결과 전체 광고 영역에서 **전환율 18.9%, 클릭률 12% 개선**을 달성했다.
items.why_it_matters: 수십억 명이 쓰는 Meta 광고 생태계 전반에 LLM식 스케일링 법칙을 적용해 실질적 비즈니스 성과로 연결시킨 사례로, 추천시스템에 트랜스포머 스케일링을 적용하는 산업적 방향성을 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존에는 Facebook, Instagram, Reels 등 서비스·목표별로 독립된 예측 시스템을 운영했으나, GEM 2026은 이를 하나의 중앙 파운데이션 모델로 대체해 전체 광고면에서 동시에 성능을 개선한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
items.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a sparsely-activated architecture that scales large language model (LLM) capacity while keeping per-token compute low. Because its operations account for a large share of total compute time, inefficiencies there directly raise request latency and cost. Therefore, optimizing MoE operations through kernel engineering offers the largest opportunity for performance gains. Fused MoE is a key optimization technique for the MoE architecture. A fused MoE system merges token routing, data shuffling, and specialized network calculations into a single batched operation on the GPU. This replaces executing those routing and expert computations as separate, sequential loop operations. While this provides latency advantages, it also brings complexity in kernel implementations and debugging capability. High GPU utilization for this architecture requires hardware-specific optimizations. In this post, we describe the different kernel optimizations we implemented for fused MoE models and show you how you can benefit from this work. We used a representative MoE model as our primary example. Swap-AB for WGMMA utilization To maximize tensor processing throughput, the NVIDIA Hopper architecture relies on the Warp Group Matrix Multiply Accumulate (WGMMA) instruction protocol, which executes collectively across a cooperative warpgroup of 128 threads. This operand asymmetry is fundamentally an instruction set architecture (ISA)-level property. In the underlying wgmma.mma_async assembly definition, the hardware fixes the matrix row dimension (M) at a constant scale of 64 to define its parallel thread-mapping topology. The column dimension (N) remains highly variable. Operand A strictly maps across this fixed M dimension (using registers or shared memory), and Operand B maps across the variable N dimension (through a shared memory descriptor). These operand slots are therefore structurally non-interchangeable. Consequently, peak hardware tile utilization is governed by these rigid shape encodings, requiring that the M dimension equals or exceeds 64 to prevent compute execution lanes from sitting idle. This structural preference stems from how Hopper Tensor Cores partition memory blocks. The hardware enforces a fixed minimum layout shape for the leading dimension of the first operand, locking the block height to exactly 64 (M=64). When a mathematical matrix possesses a large, continuous leading dimension in this primary slot, Hopper’s internal hardware schedulers can cleanly map and distribute data across the physical computing grid. This structural asymmetry becomes a severe performance bottleneck during the decode phase of MoE networks. In a standard MoE layer, the linear algebra governing expert computation is formulated using traditional matrix notation: A[M,K] x B[K,N] —> C[M,N] Where (M) represents the token row count (or batch size), (K) represents the hidden feature dimension, and (N) represents the expansive expert output dimension. During the decode phase, the system processes only one token per user sequence at a time. Consequently, the batch space or token row size is profoundly thin, regularly dropping to a profile where (M < 64), and frequently down to a single row (M = 1). Under this standard structural layout: Matrix (A) transforms into a thin, fragmented horizontal vector (for example, 1 x 4096). Matrix (B) (the core expert weights) remains in a large, dense vertical block (for example, 4096 x 8192). Because the row count (M) is tiny, Matrix (A) is physically incapable of filling the hardware’s fixed (64)-row layout bucket for Operand A. When the WGMMA instruction executes over this layout, it leaves a vast portion of the physical Tensor Core capacity completely starved. The silicon spends clock cycles processing empty spatial slots, leading to poor hardware utilization. In a standard dense LLM layer, weight matrices are static, unified, and perfectly contiguous. In an MoE layer, however, the workload is fractu
items.title_ko: AWS, SageMaker AI에서 MoE 커널 최적화 — Swap-AB로 Hopper WGMMA 활용도 개선
items.summary: 이 글은 Amazon SageMaker AI에서 Mixture-of-Experts(MoE) 모델의 연산 효율을 높이기 위한 커널 엔지니어링 기법을 다룬다. Fused MoE는 토큰 라우팅, 데이터 셔플링, 전문가 연산을 GPU 상의 단일 배치 연산으로 통합해 지연시간을 줄이지만, 커널 구현과 디버깅 복잡도가 높아진다. NVIDIA Hopper 아키텍처의 WGMMA 명령어는 행렬 M 차원을 64로 고정하는 구조적 제약이 있어, 디코드 단계처럼 토큰 배치 크기가 1에 가깝게 작아지면(M<64) 텐서 코어 자원이 크게 낭비된다. 이를 해결하기 위해 **Swap-AB** 기법으로 오퍼랜드 배치를 조정해 WGMMA 활용도를 높이는 방법을 제시한다.
items.why_it_matters: MoE 아키텍처는 LLM 용량을 키우면서도 토큰당 연산량을 낮추지만, 디코드 단계의 작은 배치 크기가 하드웨어 활용도를 떨어뜨려 **지연시간과 비용**에 직접 영향을 준다. 이런 하드웨어 특화 커널 최적화는 MoE 서빙 효율을 좌우하는 실무적으로 중요한 요소다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 순차적 라우팅·전문가 연산 루프 방식 대비, Fused MoE는 이를 단일 배치 GPU 연산으로 통합하며, 여기에 **Swap-AB**를 적용해 Hopper WGMMA의 고정된 M=64 레이아웃 제약으로 인한 텐서 코어 유휴 문제를 완화한다.

items.title: CASTLE: training natural language search before the first real query
items.abstract: How we addressed the cold-start problem for Airbnb’s natural language search by jointly generating synthetic training data — queries and relevance labels — from de-identified booking and search signals. By : Wendy Ran Wei , Hao Li , Weiwei Guo , Xiaowei Liu , Xueyin Chen , Chun How Tan , Malay Haldar , Soumyadip Banerjee , Kedar Bellare , Huiji Gao , Sanjeev Katariya , and Stephanie Moyerman Introduction Natural language search lets guests express intent in their own words, such as “romantic cabin near skiing” or “pet-friendly beach house that sleeps eight,” rather than navigating filters and categories. We needed to introduce this kind of search for Airbnb, and to have it work well from the start. However, this required training the model before we had actual user queries to train the model on, and a reasonable set of relevance labels (inferred from the queries) to map queries to matching listings. Without prior traffic, both must be synthesized from scratch. This is the cold-start problem for natural-language search. Other organizations have faced similar challenges and have created methods to address them. However, prior approaches address the need for a body of queries and the need for relevance labels separately. Passage-based methods such as InPars [1] prompt a large language model (LLM) to generate queries conditioned on a single document, then rely on additional LLM judgments to assign relevance labels, introducing a second source of error. Promptagator [2] improves query diversity using few-shot examples, but is still limited by the gap between its generation distribution and real user behavior. In this post, we describe Contrastive And Seed-guided Training for natural Language sEarch (CASTLE), our framework for jointly generating queries and producing relevance labels from Airbnb’s own de-identified booking data. Our paper describing CASTLE was accepted as a full research paper at the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management, more widely known as CIKM 2026 [3]. Challenges Generating useful synthetic training data for search requires more than producing grammatically plausible queries. The distribution of synthetic queries must match how real guests actually search; their preferred phrasing, query length, and attributes they tend to mention. If queries fail to match real-world search patterns, the model trained on them will generalize poorly. We measured this mismatch using Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence (a measure of how much one probability distribution differs from a reference distribution) between synthetic and real query distributions — both over surface-level query statistics and over attribute types (property type, amenity, location, and so on). Prior approaches scored between 9.33 and 26.2 on the KL divergence metric: far from the real-user distribution. Beyond distributional alignment, we also needed relevance labels. Generating a query is only half the problem; knowing which listings are relevant to it is the other half. Solution CASTLE addresses both challenges through a single mechanism: contrastive listing pairs derived from de-identified booking sessions, selected in accordance with user privacy permissions. When a guest books a specific listing after viewing several possible alternatives, that event implicitly encodes preference: the booked listing was selected over the others. We use these (positive, negative) pairs of listings — where the negative is randomly sampled from the other viewed-but-not-booked alternatives — as the structured input for query generation. Listing features include amenities, property details, and a one sentence summary of recent public guest reviews, with personal identifying information removed. Because we instruct the LLM to generate a query that is satisfied by the positive listing but not the negative, the relevance label is correct by construction; no post-hoc judgment is required. Crucially, what is “positive” and “negative” is determine
items.title_ko: Airbnb, CASTLE 공개 — 예약 세션 기반 합성 쿼리로 자연어 검색 콜드스타트 해결, CIKM 2026 채택
items.summary: Airbnb는 실제 사용자 쿼리가 없는 상태에서 자연어 검색 모델을 학습시켜야 하는 콜드스타트 문제를 해결하기 위해 CASTLE 프레임워크를 개발했다. 비식별화된 예약·검색 세션에서 게스트가 조회 후 예약한 리스팅(positive)과 조회만 하고 예약하지 않은 리스팅(negative)의 쌍을 추출하고, 이를 LLM에 입력해 positive는 만족하지만 negative는 만족하지 않는 쿼리를 생성하도록 지시한다. 이 방식으로 쿼리 생성과 관련성 라벨링을 동시에 해결하며, 라벨은 생성 과정 자체에서 정확성이 보장되어 별도의 사후 판정이 필요 없다. 기존 InPars, Promptagator 같은 방법은 KL divergence 기준 **9.33~26.2**로 실제 사용자 쿼리 분포와 괴리가 컸다.
items.why_it_matters: 신규 검색 기능을 실제 트래픽 없이 출시해야 하는 모든 서비스가 겪는 콜드스타트 문제에 대해, 실제 사용자 행동 데이터를 활용한 합성 학습 데이터 생성 방식을 제시한다는 점에서 실무적 참고 가치가 크다.
items.whats_different: 기존 InPars, Promptagator 같은 passage 기반 방법은 쿼리 생성과 관련성 라벨 부여를 별도 단계로 처리해 LLM 판정이라는 **추가 오차 요인**을 수반했지만, CASTLE은 예약 세션의 contrastive listing 쌍을 이용해 쿼리 생성과 라벨링을 하나의 메커니즘으로 통합한다.

items.whats_different: 기존에는 Run:ai가 NVIDIA 인수 후 상용 폐쇄형 플랫폼으로 운영되었으나, 이번 공개로 전체 플랫폼이 **오픈 파운데이션**으로 전환되어 외부 개발자와 파트너의 직접 기여 및 확장이 가능해진다.

items.title: Mix, Don't Tune: Bilingual Pre-Training Outperforms Hyperparameter Search in Data-Constrained Settings
items.abstract: For most languages of the world, language model pre-training operates in a data-constrained regime where models must repeat their training data many times, degrading generalization. Two remedies exist: aggressive hyperparameter tuning such as high weight decay, and mixing in data from a high-resource auxiliary language to directly aid the low-resource target. While hyperparameter tuning regularizes the model by shrinking weights to restrict network capacity, auxiliary data mixing uses a tunable mixing ratio to expand the training distribution and diversify the training signal with new…
items.title_ko: Apple 연구, 저자원 언어 사전학습서 하이퍼파라미터 튜닝보다 이중언어 데이터 혼합이 더 효과적
items.summary: 저자원 언어의 언어모델 사전학습은 데이터가 부족해 같은 데이터를 여러 번 반복 학습해야 하며, 이는 일반화 성능을 저하시킨다. 이를 해결하는 두 가지 방법으로 높은 weight decay 같은 공격적 하이퍼파라미터 튜닝과, 고자원 보조 언어 데이터를 섞는 방식이 있다. 하이퍼파라미터 튜닝은 가중치를 축소해 네트워크 용량을 제한하는 방식으로 규제하는 반면, **보조 데이터 혼합**은 혼합 비율을 조절해 학습 분포를 확장하고 새로운 신호로 다양성을 높인다. 데이터 제약 환경에서는 이러한 보조 언어 혼합 방식이 하이퍼파라미터 탐색보다 우수한 성능을 보인다.
items.why_it_matters: 세계 대부분의 언어는 사전학습 데이터가 부족한 상황에 놓여 있어, 이런 저자원 환경에서 효과적인 전략을 찾는 것은 다국어 모델 구축에 실질적인 영향을 미친다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 공격적 하이퍼파라미터 튜닝(높은 weight decay 등)을 통한 모델 용량 제한 방식 대비, 보조 언어 데이터를 섞어 학습 분포 자체를 확장하는 방식이 **더 나은 성능**을 보인다는 점에서 차별화된다.

items.title: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements
items.abstract: Managing AI model access across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts creates operational friction when each workload account must subscribe and accept AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers (MPPOs) individually. Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements simplifies multi-account access to third-party AI models so you can subscribe once from a central account and distribute access across your organization. In this post, we show you two ways to activate AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offer (MPPO) entitlements in AWS License Manager. Use the lightweight script when you want a one-time, no-infrastructure fix for received licenses you already trust. Use the CDK automation when you want ongoing event-driven processing that verifies sellers, creates and activates distributed grants. Why automate grant activation With AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers, you can negotiate custom rates for third-party models on Amazon Bedrock. After an eligible private offer is accepted, AWS Marketplace creates a license in AWS License Manager. In AWS Organizations with all features enabled, organization-level grants are auto-accepted but remain Disabled until you activate them. Teams often manage this by checking the AWS License Manager console and activating grants manually. Manual checks work, but they add effort and are easy to miss. Until someone activates the grant, negotiated pricing does not apply. The same effort appears as teams adopt new models or renew terms. Solution overview The sample repository provides two paths: Path 1 – The lightweight path is a standalone script that lists received licenses and prints a dry-run plan. It only creates and activates organization-wide grants when you re-run it with --apply --confirm-account-id . It has no seller allow-list, so use it only when you trust every received license in the management account. Path 2 – The event-driven path uses AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to deploy ongoing automation in your AWS management account. Choose one of the following implementation paths. Use Path 1 for one-time activation without CDK. Use Path 2 for ongoing event-driven automation. Path 1: Lightweight script (one-time activation) Use this path when you need one-time activation without deploying CDK. The script lists every received license in the management account, so use the dry run as your review gate before applying changes. Clone the sample repository locally and move into the project directory. git clone https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements.git cd sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements Run the lightweight script in dry-run mode. python3 lightweight/distribute_licenses.py Review every listed license and confirm that the ISV Partner issuer and account scope match the private offer you expect. Apply the reviewed plan from the same AWS Organizations management account. python3 lightweight/distribute_licenses.py --apply --confirm-account-id ACCOUNT_ID After the grant is active, validate the billing path before you rely on the private offer in production. Billing data in AWS Cost Explorer can lag, so use it to compare the effective charge for covered Amazon Bedrock usage after charges appear. For a repeatable check, adapt the sample scripts/bedrock_discount_check.py utility to match your ISV Partner issuer and confirm the expected discount path. Path 2: CDK automation (ongoing activation) Use this path when you want new private pricing agreements handled automatically. The CDK stack listens for eligible AWS Marketplace agreement events, checks your seller allowlist, creates distributed grants, and retries activation when License Manager needs more time. The solution contains three components: Amazon EventBridge rule : The stack listens for AWS Marketplace agreement events on the default event bus in us-east-1 . items.title_ko: AWS, Bedrock Private Pricing Offer 다중 계정 배포 자동화 — 스크립트·CDK 두 가지 경로 공개
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock에서 AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offer(MPPO)를 사용할 때, 조직 내 각 워크로드 계정이 개별적으로 구독·수락해야 하는 번거로움을 managed entitlements로 해결한다. 조직 전체 기능이 활성화된 AWS Organizations에서는 조직 수준 grant가 자동 수락되지만 기본적으로 Disabled 상태라 **수동 활성화**가 필요했다. 이를 위해 AWS는 샘플 저장소를 통해 두 가지 경로를 제공한다: 신뢰 가능한 라이선스를 일회성으로 활성화하는 경량 스크립트(dry-run 후 --apply), 그리고 판매자 허용목록을 검증하고 이벤트 기반으로 grant를 생성·재시도하는 AWS CDK 자동화다. CDK 경로는 EventBridge 규칙이 Marketplace 계약 생성 이벤트를 감지해 Lambda 함수를 호출하는 구조로 동작한다.
items.why_it_matters: 수십~수백 개 AWS 계정에 걸쳐 AI 모델 협상가를 적용하려면 grant 활성화를 누락하기 쉬운데, 활성화 전까지는 **협상된 가격이 적용되지 않아** 비용 관리에 직접적 영향을 준다. 멀티 계정 거버넌스를 운영하는 MLOps 팀이라면 모델 도입·갱신 시마다 반복되는 수작업을 줄일 수 있는 실질적 가이드다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 콘솔에서 수동으로 License Manager grant를 확인·활성화하던 방식 대비, 일회성 점검용 경량 스크립트와 판매자 검증·재시도까지 포함한 상시 이벤트 기반 CDK 자동화라는 두 가지 선택지를 제공한다.

items.title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning. We hypothesize that these failures reflect a shared deficit in visual transition reasoning, and test whether this capability can serve as a shared training primitive, one that different models can learn from different supervision sources and reuse across different tasks, with a systematic training recipe. Existing benchmarks document these deficits separately but do not support controlled comparisons across scenes, actions, and reasoning operations. We therefore introduce WOVEN, a training source and benchmark for visual transition reasoning that organizes transition supervision by scene, action, and reasoning type, using diverse, realistic rollouts from video-pretrained generative models: 36,076 examples across 20 scene types, 5 action types, and 8 reasoning types. We first evaluate 38 frontier MLLMs (e.g., GPT-5.4 and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B) and find a substantial and systematic deficit: even the strongest models fall far below humans, and the failures recur across model families and persist with scale. We then train MLLMs at multiple scales on WOVEN and find that they learn a shared capability that transfers broadly: training subsets of only about 2,000 items each collectively improve 22 of 26 external benchmarks by up to 27.3 percentage points, and WOVEN data can replace 30-50% of a task's own training data with comparable accuracy. Controlled comparisons further yield a training recipe for visual world modeling, validated prospectively on held-out benchmarks: select supervision by the reasoning operation it teaches rather than by the actions, scenes, or domains it shows, and prefer larger changes to the visual state for robustness. Our work establishes visual transition reasoning as a reusable foundation for systematic visual world-model training in MLLMs.
items.title_ko: WOVEN 공개 — 시각 전이 추론 학습으로 MLLM 외부 벤치마크 26개 중 22개 최대 27.3%p 개선
items.summary: 연구진은 MLLM이 공간·신체화·물리·시간 추론에서 겪는 실패가 '시각 전이 추론'이라는 공통 결함에서 비롯된다고 가정하고, 이를 검증하기 위해 WOVEN이라는 학습 자원 겸 벤치마크를 제안했다. WOVEN은 비디오 사전학습 생성 모델의 롤아웃을 활용해 20종 장면, 5종 행동, 8종 추론 유형으로 구성된 36,076개 예제를 포함한다. GPT-5.4, Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B 등 38개 최신 MLLM을 평가한 결과 모든 모델이 사람보다 크게 뒤처지는 결함을 보였고, 이는 모델군과 규모에 상관없이 반복됐다. WOVEN으로 여러 규모의 MLLM을 학습시키자 각 2,000개 정도의 부분집합만으로도 **26개 외부 벤치마크 중 22개가 최대 27.3%p 개선**됐으며, 기존 과제별 학습 데이터의 30~50%를 WOVEN 데이터로 대체해도 비슷한 정확도를 유지했다.
items.why_it_matters: 여러 추론 과제에 공통으로 재사용 가능한 학습 프리미티브를 발견했다는 점에서, 과제별 데이터 수집 없이도 범용 시각 세계 모델링 능력을 효율적으로 끌어올릴 수 있는 길을 제시한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 벤치마크들이 장면·행동·추론 결함을 개별적으로만 기록해 비교가 어려웠던 것과 달리, WOVEN은 장면·행동·추론 유형을 통제된 축으로 조직화해 **직접 비교**가 가능하며, 행동이나 장면이 아니라 가르치려는 추론 연산 기준으로 감독 데이터를 선택해야 한다는 학습 레시피를 제시한다.

items.title: Three Samplers, One Posterior: NUTS vs. Emcee vs. Nested Sampling
items.abstract: Benchmarking NumPyro, affine-invariant MCMC, and dynesty against exact ground truth and watching them fail. The post Three Samplers, One Posterior: NUTS vs. Emcee vs. Nested Sampling appeared first on Towards Data Science .
items.title_ko: NUTS·Emcee·Nested Sampling 비교 — 동일 사후분포 놓고 세 샘플러의 실패 지점 추적
items.summary: 이 글은 NumPyro의 NUTS, affine-invariant MCMC 기반 Emcee, dynesty의 Nested Sampling 세 가지 샘플러를 동일한 사후분포에 대해 벤치마킹한다. 정확한 **ground truth**와 비교해 각 샘플러가 언제, 어떻게 결과를 잘못 내는지를 관찰한다. 세 방법 모두 실패하는 지점이 존재함을 보여주는 사례 중심의 비교이다.
items.why_it_matters: 베이지안 추론에서 샘플러 선택은 결과의 신뢰도를 좌우하지만 실무에서는 각 도구의 한계가 잘 드러나지 않는 경우가 많다. **정확한 정답과의 직접 비교**를 통해 샘플러별 실패 양상을 구체적으로 보여주는 점이 실용적이다.

items.title_ko: 제품 데이터사이언스에서 텍스트로 이탈·CLV 모델 보강하는 실전 가이드
items.summary: 이 블로그는 고객 이탈 예측, 고객생애가치(CLV) 등 전통적인 표 기반 모델에 텍스트 데이터를 결합해 성능을 강화하는 실전적 방법을 다룬다. NLP 기법을 활용해 리뷰, 상담 로그 등 비정형 텍스트에서 특징을 추출하고 이를 기존 정형 피처와 결합하는 접근을 소개한다. 제품 데이터사이언스 맥락에서 적용 가능한 구체적인 가이드 형태로 제공된다.
items.why_it_matters: 정형 데이터만으로 한계에 부딪힌 **이탈·CLV 예측** 모델에 텍스트 신호를 추가하면 실무에서 쉽게 적용 가능한 성능 개선 경로가 될 수 있다.
